content.comment_body: I'm using a [product_name] controller and a [product_name] operator panel connected directly via ethernet (port P1 to P1). There is no external ethernet, just the controller connected to the panel. I’ve assigned the following IP addresses: Operator Panel - IP: 10.10.15.220, Subnet: 255.255.255.0, Gateway: 10.10.15.1; Controller - IP: 10.10.15.221. However, nothing is working—trying to access the controller settings results in a "Failed to Submit" error. Any advice?
Could you specify which exact [product_name] controller and operator panel you are using? Please provide the complete [article_no] for each device.
I configured my [product_name] controller and my first-generation operator panel with your suggested IP addresses and it works fine on my end.
[product_name] controller model: [article_no], [product_name] operator panel: [article_no]. This controller doesn’t have a display, so obtaining the IP directly from the device LCD isn’t possible.

The controller with [article_no] corresponds to the current model. The operator panel is a third generation device. Have you registered and selected the controller’s IP in the operator panel’s device selection menu?
Since your controller lacks a display, how did you change its IP address from 192.168.178.003 (subnet 255.255.255.000) to 10.10.15.221 (subnet 255.255.000.000)?

Background: The system worked previously but was recently relocated overseas. I suspect the controller’s IP may have changed or reset and doesn’t match the panel’s IP. Unfortunately, I don’t have access to configuration software right now. Is there another way to check the controller’s IP? Checking via operator panel settings doesn’t work due to the connection error. The controller model lacks a display, so that isn’t possible either.

Without the configuration software, you cannot change the controller’s IP address using only the operator panel. You’ll need configuration software or try using an IP scanner. You can download something like Advanced IP Scanner for free from [url].

The original IP would have been set during initial setup and things worked fine before. Changes after shipment include switching from a 240V supply to 110V (moving from NZ to USA), rewiring the power supply using a US connector ([product_name] power supply [article_no]). Power looks fine, lights are green and the PSU accepts variable voltage. It’s possible the controller was damaged during transit. I'll try to obtain the configuration software or an IP scanner.

Using an IP scanner will only help you see the controller's IP address, not change it. Changing the IP is only possible via configuration software. Do you have a backup of the controller program? If so, I could create a file for you to transfer to an mSD card containing your preferred IP settings.

I could get a copy of the program, but I can’t share it for security reasons. If I discover the controller’s IP address, can I simply adjust the operator panel’s IP settings to match so they’ll communicate properly? I appreciate the help—this is proving challenging.
If you learn the controller’s IP address using an IP scanner, you can update the operator panel settings to match the connected device’s IP.

Update: I was able to confirm the controller’s IP settings. The subnet is currently set to 255.255.255.254, which allows only one available IP—so I need to reset or adjust this to communicate with the operator panel. Is there a way to reset the IP settings without using the operator panel or my PC?
Without the configuration software, you won’t be able to proceed since your controller lacks a display.

As previously mentioned, without the configuration software, you’re unable to reset the controller’s IP if there’s no display. [company_name] offers a tool that returns the controller to its factory settings, restoring the default IP 192.168.178.003 and subnet 255.255.255.000. Copy the reset file to an mSD card, insert it into the controller, and power it off and on. Remove the mSD card after startup is complete. Look for the 'Reset Tool' for returning the controller to delivery state.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering connection issues between their [product_name] controller (which does not have a display) and operator panel over direct ethernet. Attempts to change or verify network settings have failed due to the lack of a display and configuration software, especially after relocating the equipment and changing its power supply. This leaves users unable to resolve networking errors or confirm the device’s current IP address, increasing confusion and frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want an easy way to check or reset the controller’s IP address, even without a display or access to configuration software, to reestablish connectivity.
